title: Harry Kane Wants to Try Kicking in the NFL!
summary:
Imagine you're the best soccer player in your country. You've scored 85 goals for England — more than anyone else ever. Now imagine you want to try a totally different sport: American football.

That's exactly what Harry Kane is thinking about. Kane is 33 years old and plays for Bayern Munich in Germany. He's the captain of England's national soccer team. But he says he might become an NFL kicker after he retires from soccer.

"The NFL is a lot more realistic than the golf one," Kane said. He had also talked about playing golf. But kicking in the NFL seems more possible.

Why? Because kicking a soccer penalty and kicking an NFL field goal are kind of similar. Both need a strong leg and calm nerves. "I take penalties and it is a very similar pressure and technique," Kane said.

Kane says he would practice for six months to a year before trying. He also mentioned maybe playing in MLS, the American soccer league, so he could do both sports.

Other soccer players have switched to NFL kicking. Brandon Aubrey and Jake Bates both did it. But Kane isn't leaving soccer yet — he's talking about a new contract with Bayern Munich.
why_it_matters: Kane's story shows that skills you build in one thing — like staying calm when everyone is watching — can help you try something completely new, and it's a reminder that even famous athletes keep practicing before they try a new challenge.

background_read: Harry Kane is the captain of England's national soccer team and England's all-time top scorer, and he now plays his club soccer for Bayern Munich, a top team in Germany.
Kicking is a special job in American football: most NFL teams keep one player whose main task is kicking field goals and extra points, so players who grew up playing soccer sometimes get a chance.
The NFL has been playing regular-season games in London and Germany to win new fans in Europe, which is one reason European soccer fans pay attention to American football.
Article_Structure: WHO: Harry Kane, England's captain and record scorer, who plays for Bayern Munich.
WHAT: Kane says he might try to become an NFL kicker after he retires from soccer, and he has also mentioned the American league MLS.
WHERE: He plays soccer in Germany for Bayern Munich, while the NFL is in the United States.
WHY: He says kicking a soccer penalty and kicking an NFL field goal need similar power and calm nerves, so the switch seems realistic to him.

perspectives.description: They point out that other soccer players have become NFL kickers, and Kane's strong leg and calm nerves in penalties could make him very good at it.
They say Kane still has a big job to do at Bayern Munich and England, and that NFL kicking is a totally different skill, so he should focus on soccer first.
They say switching sports is rare and hard because the ball, the timing and the pressure are all different, but players from soccer or rugby do sometimes make it as kickers.
